articles.title: Wild Horse Nine review: Malkovich and Rockwell head to Easter Island for McDonagh’s acid bromance
articles.summary: Venice film festival: Two men, some violence, much freewheeling chat: so far, so standard fare from the Oscar-winning writer-director. But this time the comedy and charm can feel diluted by blood and machismo.
body: I t isn’t a Martin McDonagh movie unless you’ve got two morose guys – one old, one not so old – who do nothing all the livelong day but bitch and snipe and quarrel and exchange barbed bromantic dialogue while occasionally going off on a plaintive tangent about nothing at all, incidentally revealing something very wrong with their friendship. If it can be called that. In The Banshees of Inisherin from 2022, the older guy decides he wants nothing more to do with the younger guy; in In Bruges from 14 years earlier (of which this latest film is almost a retread or maybe B-side), the older guy has an awful secret he is keeping from the younger guy.

articles.title: Martin McDonagh says CIA has ‘done awful things all around the world’
articles.summary: McDonagh’s new film, Wild Horse Nine, stars John Malkovich as an agent in 1970s Chile who feels ‘guilt and regret’ over his role in global interventions. The US’s history of intervening in democratic processes around the world deserves more attention in the light of current political developments…
body: “I’ve been very interested in the truth of what the CIA has been doing over the last 60 years, and the awful things they’ve done all around the world,” McDonagh said about Wild Horse Nine, his first film since his 2022 tragicomedy The Banshees of Inisherin. “I think maybe something that’s not talked about enough. We know what the KGB are like, but we probably don’t question the CIA’s activity as much as we ought to.”

In Wild Horse Nine, John Malkovich plays Chris, a veteran agent for the foreign intelligence service who is stationed in Santiago, Chile, on the eve of the US-supported coup against Salvador Allende – Latin America’s first democratically elected Marxist president – in 1973. Recently diagnosed with cancer and acting erratically, Chris is dispatched to Easter Island with his protege Lee (Sam Rockwell), where he starts to reflect critically on his role in other CIA interventions, including the Guatemalan coup d’état of 1954, the 1961 assassination of revolutionary Congolese prime minister Patrice Lumumba and – according to the film’s telling – the killing of John F Kennedy.

articles.title: ‘By Any Means’ Review: Mark Wahlberg Teaches the Virtues of Violence in Elegance Bratton’s Bluntly Drawn Historical Thriller
articles.summary: In Peter Farrelly’s “Green Book,” Viggo Mortensen’s driver famously introduces Mahersahala Ali’s concert pianist to fried chicken. The white man, an expert, proves his cultural bona fides to the Black protagonist, the student.
body: The phrase, popularized and embodied by Malcolm X, is appropriated here by Wahlberg’s mob enforcer, who teams up with a Black FBI agent played by Yahya Abdul-Mateen II.

Cut to Mark Wahlberg, muscles bulging and hair absurdly parted, in a dingy basement, beating a man to the brink of death. “Where are the bodies?” he demands, swinging a baseball bat into his bloody victim’s already pulverized knees.

So begins a streak of brutal and relentless violence taken brutally and relentlessly seriously. Based on a true story, the film tracks Wahlberg’s character, the mob enforcer Greg Scarpa, as he teams up with FBI Agent Wayne Strider, played by Yahya Abdul-Mateen II. The pair are tasked with investigating the murder of local NAACP chapter president Vernon Dahmer (Giancarlo Esposito) by members of the Ku Klux Klan — though they have starkly different ideas about how to get the job done.

articles.title: ‘Lanterns’ Episode 3 Attracts 10 Million Viewers Globally on HBO Max, a New Series High
articles.summary: HBO Max’s “Lanterns” continues to grow in viewership. The DC Studios series’ third episode, which premiered Sunday, Aug. 30, averaged 10 million viewers globally and 7 million viewers in the U.S. after three days of viewership, according to the network/streamer.
body: Episode 3 of “Lanterns” dove into the backstory of John Stewart ( Aaron Pierre ) and how long he has been preparing and training — at the direction of his parents — to one day take over the role of the Green Lantern from Hal Jordan (Kyle Chandler). In the episode, John is grilled by one of the Guardians (Laura Linney) to see whether he’s worthy of replacing Hal.
Through flashbacks, we see how his father, John Stewart, Sr. (J. Alphonse Nicholson), and mother Bernadette ( Jasmine Cephas Jones ) train him to show no fear.
Based on DC’s “Green Lantern” comic books, “Lanterns” stars Pierre, Chandler, Kelly Macdonald, Garret Dillahunt, Poorna Jagannathan, Jason Ritter and Ulrich Thomsen.

Per the official logline, the show follows “new recruit John Stewart (Pierre) and Lantern legend Hal Jordan (Chandler), two intergalactic cops drawn into a dark, earth-based mystery as they investigate a murder in the American heartland.”

articles.title: Tall tales: the 20 best giants in film – ranked!
articles.summary: On the 300th anniversary of Gulliver’s Travels, we celebrate the biggest film stars of them all – from a stone colossus to a metal-munching alien and a 50ft woman on the rampage.
body: Not a first-person-shooter BFG, alas, but one of Steven Spielberg’s worst films, reducing Roald Dahl’s story to digital pap. Mo-cap Mark Rylance, whose cutesy ungrammatical babbling should have been left on the printed page, is the 24ft Big Friendly Giant who kidnaps an orphan girl, Sophie. Ugh. Big Creepy Giant, more like.

Nicholas Hoult plays the farmhand who forms an implausible alliance with a princess in a fairytale cluttered with extraneous characters. Bill Nighy plays half of a two-headed giant, but the actors are swamped by digital effects and anti-giant propaganda. The best bit is when a massive chef rolls an extraneous Ewan McGregor in pastry and puts him in an oven.

“Stone giants!” JRR Tolkien seemingly preferred dwarves to the big people, but Peter Jackson’s three-part rendering of his stand-alone children’s classic is briefly enlivened by stone colossuses hurling boulders at each other in a thunderstorm. Though one can’t help thinking how awesome a Ray Harryhausen version might have been.

articles.title: ‘Heated Rivalry’ Season 2 Casts Milla Jovovich, Kevin Zegers and Paul Gross
articles.summary: The cast of “Heated Rivalry” continues to warm up. Kevin Zegers, Paul Gross and Milla Jovovich have joined the hit ice-hockey romance series from Crave ahead of its Season 2 debut on HBO Max in spring 2027. Zegers (“The Madison,” “Transamerica”) will play Coach Wiebe.
body: Created by Jacob Tierney, “Heated Rivalry” follows the skate-crossed love affair between rival hockey players Shane Hollander (Williams) and Ilya Rozanov (Storrie). The two star athletes are pulled together by ambition and attraction, and what begins as a secret fling between two fresh-faced rookies develops into a years-long journey of love, denial and self-discovery.

The show is based on Rachel Reid’s “Game Changers” book series, with the second season borrowing its premise from the sixth book, titled “The Long Game.” It follows Shane and Ilya as they play on teams that are closer geographically and navigate the complexities of taking their relationship public.

While “Heated Rivalry” hails from the Canadian streaming service Crave, it became a massive hit months after its U.S. debut on HBO Max. The show hit the American streamer in November 2025 but became a word-of-mouth hit in early 2026, with episodes reaching an average viewership of more than 10 million.

articles.title: Star Trek IV: The Voyage Home review – Kirk, Spock and co on semi-intentionally hilarious save-the-whale mission
articles.summary: Our heroes travel back through time to San Francisco in 1986 so they can commune with aliens threatening future Earth – it’s preposterously good fun. Here is the fourth and silliest movie in the Star Trek franchise, now on rerelease for its 40th anniversary.
body: Spock has been brought back to life, as the apparent end result of all the bizarre metempsychotic plot contortions of the previous film. But the permanent and irrevocable death of Kirk’s son seems to be passed over remarkably casually. The eerie boyishness of Shatner’s Kirk, with that beaming smile, almost makes you forget that he has been through an agonising bereavement. Hasn’t he?

A trailer released on social media gives viewers their first glimpse of the show, as well as a snippet of Zeta-Jones using her Swansea accent.

articles.summary: Amelia Dimoldenberg announces she will end her popular YouTube series after more than a decade.
body: Amelia Dimoldenberg has announced she will end Chicken Shop Date after more than a decade.
The presenter, known for her off-the-wall questions and deadpan silences, revealed the news in an Instagram post.
She has become one of the UK's best-known content creators through the web series, which features interviews with rappers, actors and celebrities framed as a "date" with the host.
While "all good dates must come to an end", Dimoldenberg told fans to expect "a few final dates" before the show officially ends.

articles.title: Harry Daniels is Done Singing at Celebrities (Maybe)
articles.summary: Dropped by UTA and dumped by a famous beau over his videos, the TikTok sensation thinks it’s time to move on from L.A. and the ambush act that made him famous.
body: Harry Daniels, the 22-year-old internet provocateur who became famous by ambushing celebrities with unsolicited serenades, says the joke may finally have run its course.

“In some ways, I no longer view myself as a person,” Daniels tells The Hollywood Reporter over an omelet at a crowded Hollywood diner. “Harry Daniels is different. I’m not Harry anymore. I’m a commodity. I’m a product.”

Daniels arrives in a Poison Candy Apple T-shirt, a friend’s clothing brand. Even under the harsh lighting of a greasy spoon, he looks younger than 22, with a full, warm smile and large hazel eyes that blink either too often or not quite enough.

He grew up on Long Island studying the mechanics of pop stardom. At 12, he was taking the train into Manhattan alone to attend showcases and waiting outside venues to meet singers. By 10th grade, he says, he was close to repeating the year because he kept skipping class for album signings.
